title: BambooHR API: Keys, Rate Limits, and Endpoints (2026)
summary: BambooHR API key generation controls your permissions and request limits. You'll understand the authentication steps and rate-limit handling.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Widening the mapping raises questions the body only touches, and most of them come back to who owns the answer when something breaks.


### Is the BambooHR API free to use?


As far as I can verify, BambooHR doesn't charge per call. Whether API access is included on every plan is a point to confirm with BambooHR before you build.


If your plan turns out to restrict it, you find out after the integration is live and someone is paged.


Get the answer in writing from your account contact, and check it against the current docs.


### Does the BambooHR API support webhooks?


BambooHR may offer webhooks, but check its documentation before relying on them; a schedule is the safer default for change detection. Polling spends your rate limit on records that didn't change. BambooHR doesn't publish that limit as a firm number.


Because webhooks only notify you of changes, you still fetch the record afterward, and you need a plan for missed deliveries.


Check the docs for which fields and events can trigger one, because that scope decides whether you can drop polling entirely or only reduce it.


### Can I write data back to BambooHR through the API?


Yes, the API accepts writes to employee records and some other areas, but a write succeeds only if the key's owner has permission to change that field.


A read-only integration can pass every test and then fail on the first write because the owner's role never allowed it.


Treat each write field as its own permission check. Log rejected writes where a named person will see them.


### What happens to my integration when the key owner leaves?


**It breaks, usually without warning** . A key is tied to the user who created it, so deactivating that account or changing their role can cut off access or quietly shrink what the key can see.


A shrunken key is worse than a dead one, because the integration keeps running and returns incomplete data.


Create keys under a dedicated service account with a named owner, record who that owner is, and put the key's rotation on a calendar.


Rotating means issuing a new key, switching the integration over, then revoking the old key. Do those steps in that order, so you never revoke the key your integration is still using.


### Is there a sandbox or test account for the BambooHR API?


Don't assume one exists on your plan. I couldn't confirm a general-purpose sandbox, so ask BambooHR directly. If you have none, test against a separate trial or non-production account, never the live one.


Use records you can afford to corrupt, because a test that writes to real employees creates a payroll or compliance problem rather than a bug report.
